transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-30
Time: 14:23 PDT
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Jared Morales (CTO, Lumen Health), Anika Patel (Head of ML), Samir Khan (Lead DevOps), Maya Ortiz (PM)
Recording: https://redwood.app/rec/ff-20260330-1423 (note: link stub)

Summary (auto):
- Redwood gave a console walkthrough focused on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdowns.
- Lumen is evaluating for a pilot for customer-facing summarization features; key concerns are cost per 1k tokens, latency SLOs, and data residency / SOC2 controls.
- Agreed next steps: share pricing/SOW, SOC2/security pack, and provision demo console + pilot scope.

--- Transcript ---
00:00 Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex Chen from Redwood, account exec, and with me is Priya Raman, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
00:07 Jared Morales: Good, thanks. Jared here. We're excited to see the console. We've been talking about ways to get more visibility into model costs.
00:12 Priya Raman: Great. Today we'll focus on the Console 






— usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and the cost breakdown features that help you understand per-route unit economics. If at any point stop me and ask questions.
00:22 Maya Ortiz: Quick ask up front, can you show multi-tenant views? We run several product lines and want to slice by team.
00:28 Priya Raman: Yep, we'll cover that. The per-route dashboards can be scoped to project, route, or team tags, and you can pin a view.
00:35 Samir Khan: Also, we need to understand whether this works with Dedicated or Private, specifically for data residency.
00:41 Alex Chen: Short answer 






— Console works across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private control planes. For the pilot we can run on Dedicated to meet isolation and residency requirements.
00:49 Priya Raman: I'll jump into the demo. (screen shares) So here is the usage analytics home. You can see aggregate tokens, requests, avg latency, errors. The top chart shows token usage over time and you can segment by model or route.
01:05 Priya Raman: Notice the dropdown to switch between billed tokens and input/output tokens 




— helps reconcile billing vs raw usage.
01:12 Anika Patel: Are those billing metrics tied to a specific pricing profile? We have different pricing for embeddings vs chat.
01:18 Priya Raman: Yes, you can attach pricing profiles per model or per route. In the cost breakdown view we translate tokens into $/K tokens using your rate card.
01:26 Jared Morales: Can you show the per-route breakdown? We have three routes: customer_summaries, internal_search, and agent_assist.
01:33 Priya Raman: Sure, switching to per-route dashboard... here. For customer_summaries you can see tokens per request, avg p95 latency, and a cost column. You can compare it to baseline run on a smaller quantized model.
01:46 (transcription note: "quantize" was sometimes transcribed as "quantized" and "quarterized")
01:51 Samir Khan: That column that says 'KV cache hit rate' 




— how is that measured? We use prefix caching heavily.
01:58 Priya Raman: It's measured at the request-router level; we instrument prefix cache hits vs misses. If you're seeing low hit rate it might be the prompt variability. We also have suggestions for batching and caching to improve unit economics.
02:12 Anika Patel: Can Redwood show us suggestions automatically? Like, tell us routes where batching would help or where we should move to a 8-bit quant model?
02:20 Priya Raman: Yes 




— Redwood Optimize gives automated recommendations. In the console we surface suggested batching window, recommended model variant (float16 vs q4f16 etc), and an estimated cost delta.
02:31 Jared Morales: Cool. For our compliance folks 




— what information is logged? We need audit trails, who called what route and what payloads were persisted.
02:39 Alex Chen: We have audit logs with request metadata and optionally payload redaction. For Private or Dedicated you can opt into full payload logging and wire it to your SIEM. We'll share the SOC2 doc with specifics.
02:49 Maya Ortiz: Is the audit log searchable? Our security team will want to query by user and by time range.
02:55 Priya Raman: Yes, logs are indexed; you can query and export. There's also token-level cost attribution so you can run chargebacks per team.
03:05 (background: faint keyboard)
03:10 Anika Patel: Regarding latency, we have a 300ms p95 SLO for the agent_assist route. Can you show latency percentiles and historical regressions?
03:18 Priya Raman: They show p50/p95/p99 and you can pin a baseline. We also correlate regressions with recent model version rollouts, kernel changes, or infra events. Here's an example where a rollout to a new quant profile increased p99, we flagged and auto-rolled back.
03:35 Jared Morales: How do rollouts work? We want canaries at 5% then ramp.
03:40 Priya Raman: Rollouts are configurable per model/route. Canary, A/B, or progressive ramp with automatic rollback on error or latency thresholds.
03:47 Samir Khan: About cost 




— can you break down cost by hardware type and model variant? We use a mix of A100 and H100 at our infra providers.
03:55 Priya Raman: In Dedicated we attach host tags so costs are split by instance type. The cost breakdown view will show tokens -> compute time -> GPU hours -> estimated dollar cost per route. We can also map to your internal cloud bill if you want.
04:08 Jared Morales: Do you have examples for sample monthly cost projections? Our CFO wants a projection on 10M tokens/month for summarization.
04:16 Alex Chen: We can run a cost projection 




— Priya, can you pull up the cost estimator?
04:20 Priya Raman: (navigates) Here's the estimator. You enter avg tokens per call and traffic patterns. For 10M tokens the estimate with a high-accuracy model is $Xk/month, with q4f16 it's roughly Y% cheaper. We'll include a sample spreadsheet in the follow-up.
04:37 Anika Patel: How accurate are those estimates 



— historically we saw mismatches with other vendors.
04:42 Priya Raman: They are based on observed token-seconds and your pricing profile; we'll run a short pilot to collect real usage and then update the projection.
04:50 Maya Ortiz: Any limitations on routing policies? We need to route EU traffic to EU-only models.
04:56 Alex Chen: Yes, smart routing supports region policies. You can set rule: if request.region == EU -> route to EU model variants or Dedicated region.
05:04 Samir Khan: From an ops perspective: what's the quickest way to try this 



— a pilot or PoC?
05:09 Alex Chen: Pilot with Dedicated is common: reserve a small pool, onboard a couple of routes, run 2 weeks of traffic for cost and latency baselining. That gives you real numbers to go to procurement.
05:19 Jared Morales: Ok that sounds good. One more technical 



— does the console surface KV cache statistics per route?
05:24 Priya Raman: Yes, hits/misses, average RTT for cache warm vs cold. Also suggestions to pre-warm hot keys. (note: "KV cache" occasionally transcribed as "K V cash")
05:35 (brief pause)
05:40 Anika Patel: Are there integrations for our internal dashboards? We use Datadog and Splunk.
05:45 Priya Raman: We have integrations and webhooks; you can export dashboards or send metrics via Prometheus, Datadog, or our audit log S3 export.
05:53 Jared Morales: Any security red flags we should be aware of with hosted vs Dedicated?
05:57 Alex Chen: Hosted is the quickest but data goes through Redwood multi-tenant environment; Dedicated isolates compute and can be VPC-peered. Private is the most restrictive where the control plane can be customer-managed. We'll surface tradeoffs in the security pack.
06:11 Maya Ortiz: Great. Can we get a sample SOW and pilot plan?
06:15 Alex Chen: Yes, I'll send a draft SOW and a proposed pilot scope.
06:19 Priya Raman: For next steps, could Samir share expected qps, token per request, and retention needs? That will let us size the Dedicated pool.
06:27 Samir Khan: I'll get that by end of week.
06:29 Alex Chen: Perfect. Quick recap: Alex sends pricing/SOW and sample spreadsheet, Priya sends SOC2/security docs and demo account, Samir and Anika provide traffic and prompt samples, then we schedule a kick-off for the pilot.
06:41 Jared Morales: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
06:43 Maya Ortiz: Thanks.
06:45 Alex Chen: Thanks all 




— we'll follow up via the CRM and send calendar for the kickoff.
06:50 (call ends)
